stories.headline: Santa Marta conference makes fossil-fuel phase-out a practical political conversation
stories.summary: IPS reports that Colombia and the Netherlands co-hosted the first Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels in Santa Marta, gathering delegates from nearly 60 nations. Rather than producing a treaty, the meeting focused on problem-solving, new work streams, scientific support, and a follow-up conference co-hosted by Ireland and Tuvalu.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a reminder to pray for leaders to move from slogans to stewardship. Creation care is not the gospel, but it is one visible arena where love of neighbour, truth-telling, and responsibility before God become concrete.

stories.headline: Kenyan community grieves death of Christian teenager after attack
stories.summary: International Christian Concern reports that a Christian teenager's death has shaken the Nguni area of Mwingi, Kenya, after Somali gunmen moved through local grazing routes near farmland. The incident follows recent violence that has left families grieving and communities unsettled.
stories.pastoral_note: Hold the persecuted church before the congregation not as distant headlines but as family. Romans 12 calls the body to weep with those who weep, and prayer is one way we refuse to let suffering believers disappear.

stories.headline: World Happiness Report spotlights youth wellbeing and social media concerns
stories.summary: The 2026 World Happiness Report examines the decline in happiness among young people in North America and Western Europe, with special attention to heavy social media use and its relationship to wellbeing, especially among girls. Canadian coverage notes Canada slipping further in the rankings amid these youth mental-health concerns.
stories.pastoral_note: The church has a discipleship opening here: not merely to scold phones, but to offer embodied community, Sabbath, intergenerational belonging, and practices that train young people to receive their life from God rather than comparison feeds.

stories.headline: Barna: many Christians are using AI for spiritual formation, while pastors feel underprepared
stories.summary: Barna's 2026 State of the Church research says nearly one in three U.S. adults view spiritual advice from AI as trustworthy as advice from a pastor, rising to two in five among Gen Z and Millennials. About four in ten practicing Christians say AI has helped them with prayer, Bible study, or spiritual growth, while only 12% of pastors feel comfortable teaching about it.
stories.pastoral_note: This calls for calm, biblical shepherding. AI can be a tool, but it must not become an oracle; pastors can help people test every voice by Scripture, community, humility, and the living presence of the Spirit.

stories.headline: HBR: high-performing teams keep improving through deliberate practices
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review's May-June 2026 feature, 'How to Build a Superteam That Keeps Getting Better,' uses the Oklahoma City Thunder's turnaround as a doorway into seven research-backed practices for building teams that continually improve rather than merely perform once.
stories.pastoral_note: Church teams need more than chemistry and goodwill. Healthy ministry cultures practice feedback, clarity, trust, and learning rhythms so gifted people become formed people serving a shared mission.

stories.headline: Fraser Valley April sales show signs of spring stability
stories.summary: Fraser Valley Real Estate Board reporting for April shows 1,118 MLS sales, up 11% from March and 7% above the same month last year. Commentary described rising sales and price gains as hints of stability as the spring market gained activity.
stories.pastoral_note: Housing remains a discipleship issue because it touches anxiety, generosity, family formation, and hospitality. Pray for wisdom for households making decisions and for the church to notice renters, young families, and those quietly priced out.

stories.headline: African youth leaders are shaping climate resilience from the ground up
stories.summary: At the UN ECOSOC Youth Forum, African climate leaders highlighted locally rooted work on water security, adaptation, advocacy, and community resilience. IPS notes that young leaders across the continent and diaspora are moving beyond awareness into practical climate leadership.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a hopeful picture of vocation: young people refusing despair and stewarding what is in their hands. It is worth blessing the next generation not only to inherit problems, but to carry courage, creativity, and faithful responsibility.

stories.headline: Survey finds viewers want more authentic faith in film and television
stories.summary: A 2026 Faith & Entertainment Index by HarrisX and the Faith and Media Initiative found that 92% of surveyed viewers say faith has a role in modern entertainment, 77% believe it can have broad appeal, and many want more accurate, complex depictions of faith rather than stereotypes.
stories.pastoral_note: This is an evangelistic doorway: people may be wary of church language, but they still recognize that stories without transcendence feel thin. Preachers can name that hunger and point from authentic human longing to the beauty of Christ.
